# YAML Configuration Standards & Cookbook

This guide serves as a central reference (or "Cookbook") for authoring Data Contracts and Configuration YAMLs in the SPARMVET project (recipe format version 1).

If you need a transformation or feature that is **not** on this list, it currently does not exist. However, you can request it through the **"Request Implementation"** button in the app! The complete list of actions, with one example each, is in `docs/appendix/transformer_actions.qmd`.

---

## 1. Schema Block Rules (Rich Dictionary Format)

Every column defined in `input_fields` or `metadata_schema` follows the **ADR-041 Rich Dictionary** format:

```yaml
column_slug:          # snake_case internal name, used for lookup and joins
  original_name: "RawColumnName"   # exact column header in the source TSV file
  type: String                     # a Polars type name, see the type table below
  label: "Human Label"             # displayed in UI filters and axis labels
```

The `column_slug` is the key the engine uses internally after renaming. `original_name` is what the ingestor looks for in your actual data file. They can differ:

```yaml
input_fields:
  sample_id:
    original_name: "SampleName"   # source file has "SampleName"
    type: String
    label: "Sample ID"
  identity_score:
    original_name: "%Identity"    # source file has "%Identity"
    type: Float64
    label: "Sequence Identity (%)"
```

Only the columns written in `input_fields` are read. A declared column that is missing from the file stops the load, and the import reports how many file columns were not declared.

### Required Properties

| Property | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | Polars type name that a text file can hold: see the table below. | `type: String` |

### Optional Properties

| Property | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `original_name` | Exact column header in the source file when it differs from the slug. Drives the rename step in the ingestor. | `original_name: "SampleName"` |
| `label` | Human-readable label for UI filters and plot axes (also the default axis title of a plot). | `label: "Sample ID"` |
| `is_entity_key` | Marks the column that identifies the entity of the table (was `is_primary_key`). Informational: join keys are written in the join step. | `is_entity_key: true` |
| `null_values`, `strip` | Override the schema's setting for this field. | `null_values: ["", "NA"]` |
| `categories` | The levels of an `Enum` field. | `categories: [low, high]` |
| `format` | Format text for `Date`, `Datetime` and `Time` fields. | `format: "%Y-%m-%d"` |
| `precision`, `scale` | Digits of a `Decimal` field. | `precision: 10` |
| `time_unit`, `time_zone` | Parameters of a `Datetime` field. | `time_unit: us` |

Every data schema also states `null_values` and `strip` (see the authoring guide): there is no default.

### Valid Types

| Type | What it is | When to use it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `String` | Text | Identifiers, free text |
| `Categorical` | Text with repeated values | Gene names, species, countries used as plot categories |
| `Int64`, `Float64` (and the other integer and float types) | Whole and decimal numbers | Percentages, scores, measurements, counts |
| `Date`, `Datetime`, `Time` | Calendar dates and times | Sampling dates, submission dates |
| `Boolean` | True/False | Resistance flags, pass/fail status |
| `Enum`, `Decimal` | Fixed list of levels; exact decimals | Ordered levels; money-like values |

> **REMOVED (recipe format 1):** the old type words `categorical`, `numeric`, `utf8`, `string`, `character`,
> `integer`, `float`, `date`, `bool` and `boolean` are refused; the message names the Polars type to write
> (`Categorical`, `Float64`, `String`, `Int64`, `Date`, `Boolean`). See `rules_data_analysis_recipe_structure.md §9`.

## 2. Wrangling Block Rules (Tiered Structure)

All wrangling logic must use the **tiered structure** (ADR-041). Every step is a registered action with the parameters its schema declares.

```yaml
wrangling:
  tier1:    # Relational foundations: runs once, shared across all plots
    - action: polars_str_strip_chars
      columns: [gene]
    - action: polars_rename
      mapping:
        old_column: new_column
  tier2:    # Reshaping: only on a schema that is plotted directly
    - action: polars_unpivot
      index: [sample_id]
      variable_name: category
      value_name: value
```

- `tier1` is required (it may be `[]`).
- `tier2` is optional. On a schema that is only an ingredient of a join, `tier2` is an error (the join has its own tiers).
- Both tiers contain **ordered lists** of action dicts. Order is deterministic.

**Identity Mode** (no wrangling needed):
```yaml
wrangling:
  tier1: []
```

---

## 3. Declarative Wrangling Actions

The engine uses a strict **Action Registry**. Only registered actions are valid, and each name carries a prefix: `polars_` (exactly the Polars call), `modif_` (a Polars idea with a documented change), `step_` (several calls). A parameter that changes the result is written in the recipe; there is no hidden default. See `docs/appendix/transformer_actions.qmd` for the complete list. The examples below were checked with the recipe checker.

### `polars_str_strip_chars`
Trims leading/trailing characters (whitespace by default) from string columns. The columns are written.
```yaml
- action: polars_str_strip_chars
  columns: [gene, predicted_phenotype]
```

### `polars_rename`
Renames columns using a mapping dict.
```yaml
- action: polars_rename
  mapping:
    old_name: new_name
    another_old: another_new
```

### `modif_filter`
Keeps rows by a comparison on one column. The rule for missing values (`na`) is required: `keep` or `remove`. `op` is one of `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, `le`, `in`, `not_in`, `between`.
```yaml
- action: modif_filter
  column: identity
  op: between
  value: [90, 100]
  na: remove
```

### `polars_drop`
Removes columns from the dataframe (a column that is not there stops the step).
```yaml
- action: polars_drop
  columns: [host_animal_common, internal_flag]
```

### `polars_select`
Keeps only the listed columns, in this order (drops all others). As the last step of a join's tier 1 it publishes the columns of the table.
```yaml
- action: polars_select
  exprs: [sample_id, gene, predicted_phenotype]
```

### `polars_fill_null`
Replaces missing values with a value (or a Polars strategy).
```yaml
- action: polars_fill_null
  columns: [predicted_phenotype]
  value: "Unknown"
```

### `polars_str_replace_all`
Replaces a pattern in text columns.
```yaml
- action: polars_str_replace_all
  columns: [source]
  pattern: "unknown"
  value: "Unknown"
  literal: true
```

### `polars_str_split` then `polars_explode`
Splits a delimited string column into a list, then explodes it into one row per value. **Warning: inflates row count.**
```yaml
- action: polars_str_split
  columns: [virulence_raw]
  by: ","
- action: polars_explode
  columns: [virulence_raw]
```

### `polars_unpivot`
Reshapes wide-format data to long format (formerly `melt`).
```yaml
- action: polars_unpivot
  index: [sample_id, ST]
  variable_name: category
  value_name: value
```

### `polars_unique`
Removes duplicate rows over `subset`. `keep` and `maintain_order` are required: the order rule is part of the recipe.
```yaml
- action: polars_unique
  subset: [sample_id, gene]
  keep: first
  maintain_order: true
```

### `polars_join` (join steps only)
Joins a right ingredient into the base frame. Quote `'on'`: unquoted, YAML parses it as the boolean `True` (the YAML boolean trap, see `rules_data_analysis_recipe_structure.md §7`). `on` is a list; `how` and `maintain_order` are required.
```yaml
- action: polars_join
  right_ingredient: sample_metadata
  'on': [sample_id]
  how: left              # left | inner | full | semi | anti ...
  maintain_order: left_right
```
Asymmetric keys:
```yaml
- action: polars_join
  right_ingredient: sample_metadata
  left_on: [isolate_id]
  right_on: [sample_id]
  how: left
  maintain_order: left_right
```

> **REMOVED (recipe format 1):** `derive_categories`, `split_and_explode`, `split_column`, `drop_duplicates`,
> `unique_rows`, `strip_whitespace`, `keep_columns`, `drop_columns`, `fill_nulls`, `replace_values` and `filter_range`
> are no longer actions. A lookup against a reference table is a `polars_join` with the table as an ingredient.

## 4. Join Block Rules

The `joins` block defines how wrangled datasets are joined into a single analysis frame.

```yaml
joins:
  AMR_Profile_Joint:
    label: "AMR profile"
    ingredients:
      - dataset_id: amr_data
      - dataset_id: sample_metadata
    steps: !include 2_test_data_ST22_dummy/wrangling/AMR_Profile_Joint.yaml
    labels:
      Year: "Year of sampling"
```

- `ingredients` is a **list of dicts** with `dataset_id` keys (not a flat list of strings).
- `steps` holds the tier lists (`tier1`, optional `tier2`) and may be inline or `!include`-ed.
- The published columns are the last step of `tier1` (a plain `polars_select` or `polars_drop`). There is no `final_contract`.
- `labels` is a `{column: text}` mapping of display names (display only).

---

## 5. Fragment Files and `!include`

Large data analysis recipes can be split into fragment files using `!include`:

```yaml
# In master_data_analysis_recipe.yaml
data_schemas:
  amr_data:
    source:
      type: local_tsv
      path: assets/test_data/amr_results.tsv
    input_fields: !include fragments/amr_input_fields.yaml
    wrangling: !include fragments/amr_wrangling.yaml
```

Fragment files **may optionally include their wrapper key** at the top level; the engine automatically unwraps it:

```yaml
# amr_input_fields.yaml: both formats are valid:

# Option A (flat, no wrapper):
sample_id:
  original_name: sample_id
  type: String
  label: Sample ID

# Option B (wrapped, engine strips the key automatically):
input_fields:
  sample_id:
    original_name: sample_id
    type: String
    label: Sample ID
```

The `!include` path is always **relative to the master data analysis recipe file's directory**, and may not reach outside the project.
